mission.title: Something Wicked
mission.description: Ask the Apothecary how to make the Oracle's termination code, and bring her a sample of the Oracle's code taken from Sati.

npc.say: Ahem... There was a minor misunderstanding. I believe it was resolved to our guest's...satisfaction.
An elegant solution, I think. How convenient that our new ally already has the target's ward in his possession, mm?
A study of the Ars Moriendi might be appropriate at this juncture, operative. It is an oft-neglected field.

phase.briefing:
The Apothecary has been brought into the Matrix by the Trainman, {player}, and her long vacation in the Machine mainframes does not appear to have damaged her morbid attitude. One does come to prize unique personalities after having spent so many years surrounded by banal operatives...
You'll find her well-guarded by our programs. You're to enquire how we should proceed with the manufacture of the Oracle's termination code, given that we already have one of the Machine cheat codes.
Oh, and if you want to leave with your RSI intact, I suggest being polite.

enter.say:
Got Exile programs in there... One of them's a big one. I'm thinkin' that's probably the Apothecary.
So, she and Persephone used to hang out back in the day... I wonder if she's equally va-va-voom?

talk.say: I require a sample of the target's code--something they wear, make, or shed.

done.say:
I don't know if the Oracle sheds...
Am I the only one a little freaked out by this chick?

near.say: Hey, that's one of our vamps down. What's going on? I don't see any hostiles on my screen.

phase.briefing:
Still among the living, operative? Ah... I suppose we must continue, then.
Our field team brain trust has come up with an idea or two on how we can acquire some of the Oracle's code for the Apothecary, I believe; and no, it does not involve shedding.

enter.say:
So, I'm just gonna throw this out there...
What if she kills us all? Well, you all? I'm serious! I'm telling you, something about this feels wrong. That lady is baaad news.
Hrmph. Anyway, Malphas is in there, and I think your favorite octogenarian hologram.

talk.say:
The solution to this problem may be quite simple. The General holds captive Sati, the Oracle's ward. As everyone knows, the Oracle and Sati frequently bake together in the Oracle's apartment. The cookies they produce are known to have unique properties; they are, of course, programs written by the Oracle.
Furthermore, it is known that Sati herself consumes these items frequently, executing their embedded code. The Oracle's purpose in feeding Sati a constant supply of these codes is not known, but that is not a concern at the moment. What is important is that Sati's own code structure has absorbed a significant amount of this Oracle code. Therefore, a sample taken from Sati should meet the Apothecary's requirements. The General will direct you to the child.

Yes, soldier. My men are escorting Sati into the Matrix as we speak. Because of her strategic value, I can keep her here only briefly. My technicians will extract the necessary sample from her, and hand it off to you. Your operator will be provided with the location as soon as you're ready to go.

phase.briefing:
I have my doubts about this "plan." Do we trust the General to operate on Sati? I suppose we have little choice at the moment--and he's kept her intact this long, hasn't he? Maybe the old warhorse has developed a soft spot in the skull for the girl.
Off you trot, operative. Get that code sample for the Apothecary, and I'm sure the two of you will become great chums.

enter.say: Let's see: commandos, technician routines, and...ah! That spot of digital sunshine I see there has got to be Sati. Poor kid. It must be like getting her wisdom teeth out.

done.say:
What?! They're not gonna let us in to see Sati? Grrr... Seems to me the General's forgetting who's buttering his waffles these days...
Fine. That technician better have something good.

talk.say: Yes, I have the data sampled from Sati here. I think you'll find it up to spec.

done.say:
Remind me not to invite these guys to any parties.
Better get that data from him.
At least Flood should be pleased. Wait, what am I saying?

objective.text: Get the data from Gaston Johansen

done.say: You know, if we're gonna be helping the commandos out, we'll need to have a serious sit-down with them about some of their "regulations." They're startin' to cramp my style...

near.say: Far door's sealed off. Looks like they aren't taking any chances with the Machines or Zion getting their hands on Sati. Try talking to that commando guard.

phase.briefing:
Complain about the commandos all you like, operative; it only reminds me how refreshing it is to have people around who actually know how to keep their mouths shut and follow orders.
Maybe that's why the Apothecary strikes my strained sensibilities as such breath of spring air: quiet, slaughters morons, doesn't smell...

enter.say:
Hey, you don't smell anywhere near as bad as Ookami does. Usually. I'll back you up on that.
Okay, looks like we've got the Apothecary and Malphas as the two main blips on the radar. Now there's a cute couple...

objective.text: Give the data to the Apothecary

done.say: So... She's cool with that, right? Not gonna kill us with a glance or anything?

Oh, man. She's gonna kill us. Come on, you can see it in her eyes!
Look, tell Malphas. He'll know what to do.

talk.say: Mm... Our data is in the hands of an expert--an artist, even--in the medium of death. To watch her at work is inspirational...and also highly dangerous. It will not be long now before the Merovingian has the weapon he seeks.

done.say:
...Or before we're all dead!
Nobody ever listens to me...

mission.finish:
Fascinating creature! Be still my heart.
I'm speaking of the Apothecary, imbecile. And not literally. What heart I may have is mine, and mine alone.
Oh, for crying out-- Have you never heard of poetry, operative? Alas, the waste I make of my time and talents...
